en.html:
Without warning, I felt a gaze on me and looked up.

I surveyed the room. No one.

Nothing had changed from before I began reading the paper.

...Had I imagined it?

I lowered my eyes to the paper again. Where had I reached? I tried to follow the text, and suddenly found a scrawl.

In a corner of the page, a rough hand quite unlike the main text. It did seem to be the same person's handwriting, though.

The language was different too. English and Yamato mingled in the main text; the scrawl was <ruby>the German language<rt>German</rt></ruby>.

A single sentence, apparently written in one rush.

Mein... Machthabar...
Kristallnacht...

Years ago, while desperately seeking a cure for my sister's illness, I had nibblednibbled at German, the language of a country advanced in medicine. I turned my unreliable memory upside down and scraped the bottom. Somehow I put together a translation that made sense.

'My Great Law-Head, what happened on the Night of Crystal?'

en.html:
A girl.

Since when had she been there?

Only a few dozen seconds ago, when I looked around the room, surely she had not been there. But had she? It was possible that I had <ruby>looked at her and still overlooked her<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.

Even that absurd possibility had to be considered. So completely did the girl lack any 'assertion.' An assertion that she was here. That she was an individual. None.

Hardly anything resembling a human presence came from her. For someone with blood flowing and a heart beating, she was much too inorganic.

I entertained the absurd idea. Even that, however, I could not dismiss outright. The girl's stillness and lack of movement exceeded all ordinary limits.

Slowly, I extended a finger and touched her cheek.

Soft.
Warm.

Skin with body heat. Yes, she did seem to be a properly living human being.

A voice meant nothing, but touch might serve as a stimulus: the girl blinked. Then she gazed steadily up at me.

On and on.

Wolf"One doubt has been living very comfortably in my mind for years."
Kageaki"What doubt?"
Wolf"This business of speaking correctly. What is humanity getting out of it?"
Kageaki"...You mean in the philosophical sense?"
Wolf"That description will do. But zara socho—nobody enters the world with command of the subjunctive. Afterward we are learning it, practicing it, making such efforts to get everything correct."
Wolf"Wherever you look, almost everyone is doing this. As though destiny had signed us all up for correct speech."
Wolf"Then we become excited, and what comes out? Noise! Glorious noise, answerable to no grammar. First get correct, then get happy, and correctness has already left. What is the sense in this arrangement?"
Kageaki"Some people do without correct speech from the beginning."
Wolf"Yes, and what do we call them? Violators! Incorrect against a correct society. Our rule remains; they have not escaped it."
Kageaki"For particular tastes, then."
Wolf"But the ordinary people abandon it eventually too. If everyone is going there, why make such elaborate preparations to start somewhere else?"
Wolf"I say let humanity not begin this correctness business at all! No preparation, no eventual undoing. The whole arrangement is unnecessary!"

Kageaki"...I see. I understand the point."
Wolf"Good. Then you are with me."
Kageaki"No."
Wolf"NO!?"
Kageaki"People should speak correctly."
Wolf"Why?"
Kageaki"This time, let me ask you something."
Wolf"Go on."
Kageaki"Suppose someone spoke nothing but incomprehensible nonsense to you. Would that make you happy?"
Wolf"Are you trying to insult me?"
Kageaki"Please answer."
Wolf"I would inform him, at considerable volume, that making sounds is not the same as making sense. Then demand one sentence fit for human use!"
Kageaki"So you would have to correct him. Would you enjoy that work?"
Wolf"Enjoy? Already I am tired, and the fellow is not even here!"
Kageaki"The reverse, then. Take a fine, proper sentence and make a wreck of it. By choice."
Wolf"Wah! That is life giving you its best part."
Kageaki"There you have it."
Wolf"Have what?"
Kageaki"If everyone talks nonsense, you must keep repairing other people's sentences. If people ordinarily speak properly, you can choose a particularly fine sentence and ruin it at your leisure. Which life would you choose?"
Kageaki"Surely that much is clear."
Wolf"————————"
Wolf"OHH!!"

Kageaki"Please answer."
Wolf"I would inform him, at considerable volume, that making sounds is not the same as making sense. Then demand one sentence fit for human use!"
Kageaki"So you would have to correct him. Would you enjoy that work?"
Wolf"Enjoy? Already I am tired, and the fellow is not even here!"
Kageaki"The reverse, then. Take a fine, proper sentence and make a wreck of it. By choice."
Wolf"Wah! That is life giving you its best part."
Kageaki"There you have it."
Wolf"Have what?"
Kageaki"If everyone talks nonsense, you must keep repairing other people's sentences. If people ordinarily speak properly, you can choose a particularly fine sentence and ruin it at your leisure. Which life would you choose?"
Kageaki"Surely that much is clear."
Wolf"————————"
Wolf"OHH!!"

en.html:
Kageaki"...At present, I consider my treatment reasonably proper for a prisoner. Therefore, I have no intention of active hostility."
Kageaki"Unless your request would seriously disadvantage me or those connected with me, Professor, I shall do what I can within my means."
Wolf"Yes, yes. Nothing so grand, really."
Wolf"A small matter. Immediately settled."
Kageaki"...Sir."
Wolf"Are you healthy?"
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"Yes. On the whole, my bodily functions present no difficulty."
Wolf"No chance of finding that you have accidentally dropped dead by tomorrow morning?"
Kageaki"...I should think not."
Wolf"Good. Business concluded. You may return to your room."
Wolf"The soldier who brought you here is waiting outside."
